experiences.description: Visit the ancient pre-Aztec city of Teotihuacan, climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Moon, and explore the Avenue of the Dead. On the way back, stop at a local roadside stand for authentic barbacoa tacos and pulque.
experiences.location: Teotihuacan, State of Mexico (day trip from CDMX)

experiences.name: Coyoacán Neighborhood Walk & Frida Kahlo Museum
experiences.description: Stroll through the cobblestone streets of bohemian Coyoacán, visit the iconic Casa Azul (Frida Kahlo Museum), browse the local artisan market, and enjoy a traditional Mexican lunch at a neighborhood fondita.

experiences.name: Taco Crawl in La Condesa & Roma

experiences.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes & Historic Center Walking Tour

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 13:00. Use the morning to rest on the plane and prepare for arrival. Take the Metro Line 1 (pink) from Aeropuerto station to the city center for only ~5 MXN – the most budget-friendly airport transfer available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique stay in Centro Histórico, freshen up, then take a self-guided walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución) – Mexico City's massive main square. Admire the Metropolitan Cathedral (free entry), watch street performers, and soak in the energy of the historic center. Pop into the Palacio Nacional to see Diego Rivera's stunning murals for free.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Calle Regina – a lively pedestrian street just south of the Zócalo – lined with street food vendors, bars, and local life. Explore the surrounding streets of Centro Histórico as they light up at night.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport.
meals.lunch: Head to Mercado de San Juan Arcos de Belén or a nearby taquería near the Zócalo. Try tacos de canasta or tacos al pastor for 15–25 MXN each.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a comedor (small local eatery) on Calle Regina or nearby. Look for a 'Comida Corrida' set menu (soup, main, drink) for around 80–120 MXN. Try enchiladas or a hearty bowl of pozole.

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first afternoon light – jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport (avoid large exchanges there) and use ATMs in the city center for better rates. Keep belongings secure in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Start early at Mercado de la Merced, one of the largest traditional markets in Latin America, just a short walk from Centro Histórico. Wander through stalls of fresh produce, spices, dried chiles, and local snacks. This is a true slice of everyday Mexico City life. Grab a fresh juice and tamales from market vendors for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Templo Mayor archaeological site (entry ~80 MXN with student discount, ~100 MXN standard) – the ruins of the great Aztec temple right in the heart of the city. The on-site museum is included in the ticket and is world-class. Afterward, walk to the nearby Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire its stunning Art Nouveau/Art Deco exterior for free, and peek inside the lobby.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Barrio Chino (Chinatown) on Calle Dolores, just a few blocks from Bellas Artes. Browse the colorful street stalls and enjoy the quirky mix of Mexican and Chinese culture. Then head back toward the Zócalo for a relaxed evening walk.

meals.breakfast: Tamales and atole (warm corn drink) from a street vendor at Mercado de la Merced – around 30–50 MXN total.
meals.lunch: Tortas or tostadas from a market stall near Templo Mayor – budget 50–80 MXN for a filling meal.
meals.dinner: Try a local fondita (home-style restaurant) near your hotel. Order mole negro with rice and beans, a classic Mexico City dish, for around 80–130 MXN. Ask locals for their favorite spot.

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays, so Tuesday is perfect. Bring a light jacket – March evenings in Mexico City can be cool at 2,240m altitude. Student ID cards can get discounts at many museums.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro (Line 3, green) to Coyoacán – a charming, bohemian neighborhood about 30 minutes from Centro. Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul) – book tickets online in advance as they sell out (entry ~270 MXN, worth every peso). Arrive right when it opens to beat crowds. Explore the cobblestone streets and colorful colonial architecture around the museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Coyoacán's main square (Jardín Centenario) and enjoy the relaxed, village-like atmosphere. Browse the weekend-style artisan market stalls for crafts and souvenirs. Visit the nearby Mercado de Coyoacán for an authentic street food lunch. Then take the Metro back toward Centro or continue to the UNAM campus area to see the stunning mosaic-covered Central Library (free, outdoor viewing).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico and visit Plaza Garibaldi at dusk – the famous Mariachi square where bands serenade visitors and locals alike. Enjoy the festive atmosphere. You can tip a band to play a song (around 100–150 MXN per song) or simply enjoy the ambient music for free.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast near your hotel before heading out – a torta or quesadilla from a street cart for 30–50 MXN.
meals.lunch: Tostadas de tinga or sopes at Mercado de Coyoacán – one of the best street food markets in the city. Budget 60–100 MXN for a satisfying spread.
meals.dinner: Pulque bar experience near Plaza Garibaldi – try this ancient fermented agave drink (15–25 MXN per cup) alongside botanas (free snacks). Grab street tacos nearby for dinner, around 60–90 MXN for 3–4 tacos.

day_by_day.notes: The Metro is the cheapest and fastest way to get around – single ride is ~5 MXN. Coyoacán is very walkable once you arrive. Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets at least a few days in advance online at museofridakahlo.org.mx.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro (Line 2, blue) to Bellas Artes, then walk north into Barrio Tepito and Santa María la Ribera neighborhoods to experience working-class Mexico City culture. Visit the Museo del Chopo (entry ~30 MXN) – a beautiful iron-and-glass Gothic building housing contemporary and alternative art exhibitions. Then head to Parque Sullivan where local artists display their work on weekends (check if active on Thursdays).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec Park (entry ~85 MXN) – arguably one of the greatest museums in the world. It houses the famous Aztec Sun Stone and extraordinary pre-Columbian collections. Spend 2–3 hours here. Afterward, stroll through Bosque de Chapultepec (free) – the massive urban park beloved by locals for picnics, exercise, and weekend relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or take the Metro to Colonia Roma Norte – a trendy but still accessible neighborhood. Explore Álvaro Obregón Avenue lined with street art, hip cafés, and local restaurants. Browse the neighborhood's beautiful Art Deco and Porfirian architecture at golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Chilaquiles (tortilla chips simmered in salsa) at a local café near your hotel – a classic Mexico City breakfast for 60–90 MXN.
meals.lunch: Pack a snack from a market or grab elotes (grilled corn) and aguas frescas from Chapultepec Park vendors for around 40–60 MXN.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Colonia Roma – find a taquería serving tacos de suadero or carnitas. Many spots offer tacos for 20–30 MXN each. Budget 80–120 MXN for a full dinner with a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Sundays at the Museo Nacional de Antropología are free for Mexican nationals but may still charge tourists. Chapultepec Park is always free. Keep an eye on your belongings on the Metro during rush hours (7–9am and 6–8pm).

day_by_day.morning: Spend your final morning revisiting your favorite spots in Centro Histórico. Visit the Mercado de Artesanías (craft market) near the Ciudadela for last-minute souvenirs – this is one of the best and most affordable places to buy authentic Mexican crafts, textiles, and pottery. Practice your bargaining skills! Also visit the nearby Biblioteca de México (free) housed in a stunning colonial building.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to La Lagunilla Flea Market (free to browse) – a sprawling antique and secondhand market north of the Zócalo where you can find vintage items, old Mexican art, books, and curiosities. Soak up the authentic local atmosphere on your last afternoon. Return to your hotel, pack up, and take a final walk around the Zócalo to say goodbye to the city.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your last night with a special but still budget-friendly dinner. Head to a traditional cantina in Centro Histórico – try Cantina La Peninsular or a similar historic spot. Order a mezcal or craft beer and enjoy botanas (free bar snacks). End the evening with a final walk under the illuminated Zócalo and Metropolitan Cathedral.

meals.breakfast: Café de olla (traditional spiced coffee) and pan dulce (sweet bread) from a panadería (bakery) near your hotel – around 30–50 MXN.
meals.lunch: Street tacos or a torta from a vendor near La Lagunilla market – budget 50–80 MXN.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a traditional cantina – a meal with drinks for around 150–200 MXN. Splurge slightly on this last night to celebrate a great trip!

day_by_day.notes: Keep your departure logistics in mind – confirm your checkout time and plan your airport transfer in advance. The Metro to the airport is the cheapest option (Line 5, yellow, from Pantitlán). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for international departures. Overall daily budget estimate: 300–500 MXN (~$15–25 USD) per day excluding accommodation is very achievable in Mexico City.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Check in to your boutique hotel in Centro Histórico, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll through the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Admire the Metropolitan Cathedral and the National Palace façade from the outside. Walk along Madero Street, a vibrant pedestrian corridor lined with historic buildings, street performers, and local vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the illuminated Zócalo at dusk — the square takes on a magical atmosphere after dark. Head to a nearby cantina or mezcal bar in the Centro for a relaxed first evening, soaking in the local ambiance.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Mercado de San Juan Arcos de Belén — a beloved indoor market a short walk from the hotel. Try tacos de canasta, fresh juices, and traditional antojitos at one of the market stalls. Budget: ~$5–10 USD.
meals.dinner: El Cardenal (Centro Histórico branch) — a classic Mexico City institution serving traditional Mexican cuisine. Try the mole, chiles en nogada (seasonal), or classic soups. Mid-range pricing: ~$20–30 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 starts post-arrival. Keep it light and walkable — everything is within easy reach of your hotel. Exchange some cash or use ATMs near the Zócalo for local spending.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Templo Mayor Archaeological Site and Museum, located steps from the Zócalo. This ancient Aztec temple complex is one of Mexico City's most important cultural landmarks. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the ruins and the excellent on-site museum filled with pre-Columbian artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Palacio Nacional (National Palace) to see Diego Rivera's legendary murals depicting Mexican history — free entry. Afterward, walk to the Barrio de la Merced area and explore La Merced Market, one of the largest traditional markets in the city, bursting with produce, spices, street food, and local life.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance or cultural event at the Palacio de Bellas Artes — check the schedule in advance for ballet folklórico, opera, or art exhibitions. Even if no performance is scheduled, the exterior and lobby are breathtaking and worth a visit at night.

meals.breakfast: Café de Tacuba — a historic café operating since 1912, just blocks from the hotel. Try tamales, atole, and café de olla (traditional clay-pot coffee). Budget: ~$8–12 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat at the food stalls inside La Merced Market — try pozole, enchiladas, or fresh tortas from local vendors. Authentic and affordable: ~$4–8 USD.
meals.dinner: Azul Histórico — a stylish courtyard restaurant in Centro Histórico serving elevated traditional Mexican dishes. Great for a mid-range splurge. ~$25–35 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor entry is around $5–7 USD. Palacio Nacional is free. Bellas Artes performances vary in price — book tickets online in advance if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short metro or Uber ride to Coyoacán neighborhood. Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul) — book tickets online well in advance as they sell out quickly. Explore the colorful colonial-era home and garden that was Frida's birthplace and studio.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through Coyoacán's charming cobblestone streets and central plaza (Jardín Centenario). Browse artisan markets, pop into local galleries, and visit the Leon Trotsky Museum nearby for an additional cultural layer. Return to Centro Histórico by late afternoon via metro or Uber.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Garibaldi Plaza in the evening — the famous gathering spot for mariachi bands. Enjoy live music, street performers, and the festive atmosphere. Sip a tequila or mezcal at one of the surrounding pulquerías or cantinas.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel or a nearby café in Centro before heading out. Try a local panadería (bakery) for pan dulce and coffee. Budget: ~$4–7 USD.
meals.lunch: Mercado de Coyoacán food stalls — try tostadas de tinga, enchiladas, and fresh agua fresca. A beloved local lunch spot. Budget: ~$5–10 USD.
meals.dinner: Near Garibaldi — try Salón Tenampa, a legendary cantina with live mariachi. Order traditional dishes like birria or carnitas alongside a margarita. ~$15–25 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance at museofridakahlo.org.mx. Metro Line 3 connects Centro to Coyoacán (Viveros station) cheaply and efficiently.

day_by_day.morning: Take an Uber or organized tour to Teotihuacán, the ancient pre-Aztec city of pyramids, about 50 km northeast of the city (roughly 1 hour by car). Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon, and walk the Avenue of the Dead. Arrive early to beat the crowds and heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City by early afternoon. Stop in the Roma Norte or Condesa neighborhood on the way back — two of the city's trendiest districts. Stroll tree-lined Álvaro Obregón Avenue, browse independent bookshops, boutiques, and street art.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the vibrant nightlife of Roma Norte — the neighborhood comes alive at night with mezcalerías, craft cocktail bars, and live music venues. A perfect evening for bar-hopping at a relaxed pace.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks or eat a light breakfast before departing early for Teotihuacán. Alternatively, grab street tacos near the archaeological site entrance upon arrival.
meals.lunch: La Gruta Restaurant at Teotihuacán — a unique dining experience inside a natural cave near the pyramids. Traditional Mexican cuisine in a spectacular setting. ~$20–30 USD per person.
meals.dinner: Contramar (Roma Norte) — one of Mexico City's most celebrated seafood restaurants, famous for its tuna tostadas and red-and-green grilled fish. Reserve ahead. ~$25–40 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Teotihuacán entry is approximately $5–7 USD. Consider hiring a guide at the site for deeper cultural context (~$20–30 USD for a 2-hour tour). Wear sunscreen and comfortable shoes for the pyramids.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology) in Chapultepec — one of the finest museums in Latin America, housing the famous Aztec Sun Stone and vast pre-Columbian collections. Allow at least 2–3 hours to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Bosque de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Forest), Mexico City's beloved urban park. Visit Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec) for panoramic city views and Mexican history exhibits. Wind down with a walk along the park's paths and lakes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico for a final evening. Revisit the Zócalo one last time, pick up souvenirs from artisan shops near the cathedral, and enjoy a farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant with views of the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Fonda Margarita (Benito Juárez neighborhood, short Uber ride) — a legendary no-frills breakfast spot beloved by locals. Try huevos con frijoles and fresh-squeezed juice. Opens early; cash only. Budget: ~$5–8 USD.
meals.lunch: Lalo! (Roma Norte) — a popular brunch and lunch spot with creative Mexican dishes, excellent coffee, and a lively atmosphere. ~$12–18 USD per person.
meals.dinner: Balcón del Zócalo (rooftop of the Holiday Inn, Centro Histórico) — spectacular views of the Zócalo and Metropolitan Cathedral with solid traditional Mexican cuisine. A memorable final dinner. ~$25–40 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Museum of Anthropology entry is approximately $5 USD; free on Sundays. Chapultepec Castle entry is around $4 USD. Keep the last evening relaxed — pack bags tonight if departing the next morning.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer from Benito Juárez International Airport to your boutique hotel in Centro Histórico. Settle in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity arranged by the concierge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through the heart of Centro Histórico. Stroll the iconic Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), admire the façade of the Palacio Nacional, and step inside the Metropolitan Cathedral. End the walk at the nearby Templo Mayor archaeological site for a curated private guided tour of the Aztec ruins.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the rooftop terrace of a nearby luxury bar overlooking the Zócalo skyline — try Bar La Opera or the rooftop at Hotel Zócalo Central. Follow with a private tasting-menu dinner at Azul Histórico, celebrated for its refined regional Mexican cuisine served in a stunning colonial courtyard.

meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at the hotel or a nearby café such as Café de Tacuba, one of Mexico City's oldest and most storied dining institutions
meals.dinner: Azul Histórico — elevated Mexican cuisine in a colonial courtyard setting; reserve the chef's tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Ask the hotel concierge to pre-book Templo Mayor tickets and dinner reservation. Pace Day 1 lightly to allow for jet lag adjustment.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Palacio Nacional to view Diego Rivera's monumental murals depicting Mexican history. Afterward, explore the adjacent Palacio de Bellas Artes, a UNESCO-recognized masterpiece of Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture, and browse its world-class fine art collection inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the vibrant neighborhood of Colonia Roma (20-minute private car ride) for a premium food and culture deep-dive. Join a curated small-group or private culinary walking tour led by a local chef, sampling street tacos, artisanal mezcal, heirloom chocolate, and traditional antojitos at carefully vetted stops. Visit the Mercado de Medellín for an authentic local market experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico for dinner at Contramar (or its sister concept), followed by after-dinner drinks at Licorería Limantour — consistently ranked among the world's best bars — for expertly crafted Mexican-inspired cocktails.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or a visit to Panadería Rosetta in Colonia Roma for artisan pastries and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Tasting stops during the culinary walking tour in Colonia Roma — a curated progression of local bites and drinks
meals.dinner: Contramar — iconic Mexico City seafood institution beloved by locals and food lovers alike; reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Book the private Palacio Nacional tour with a licensed art historian guide for deeper context. Confirm culinary tour booking at least 48 hours ahead. Dress code at Licorería Limantour is smart casual.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to Teotihuacán, the ancient pre-Columbian city of pyramids located about 50 km northeast of Mexico City (45-minute private transfer). Enjoy an exclusive early-access visit before the crowds arrive, climbing the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon with a specialist archaeologist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and check into a spa treatment at your hotel or a nearby luxury wellness center — the Four Seasons Mexico City spa is an excellent option for a traditional temascal (pre-Hispanic steam ceremony) or a deep-tissue massage. Spend the remainder of the afternoon at leisure exploring the antique shops and galleries around the historic Barrio Antiguo.
day_by_day.evening: Reserve a table at Pujol, consistently ranked among the world's top 20 restaurants. Chef Enrique Olvera's legendary Mole Madre — a mole aged over 1,000 days — is a once-in-a-lifetime culinary experience. Pair with the full beverage program featuring rare Mexican wines and spirits.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the Teotihuacán departure (depart by 7:30 AM recommended)
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at La Gruta — a dramatic restaurant set inside a natural cave adjacent to the Teotihuacán site, serving classic Mexican dishes
meals.dinner: Pujol — one of Mexico's most celebrated fine-dining restaurants; book 4–6 weeks in advance; opt for the full tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Depart for Teotihuacán no later than 7:30 AM to maximize early access and avoid midday heat and crowds. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sun protection. Pujol is located in Polanco — arrange a private car for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the world-renowned Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec Park — one of the greatest anthropological museums on earth. Arrange a private expert-guided tour (2–3 hours) focusing on Aztec, Maya, and Olmec civilizations. Stroll through the lush Bosque de Chapultepec afterward.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Polanco neighborhood — Mexico City's answer to Beverly Hills. Browse the high-end boutiques along Presidente Masaryk Avenue, visit the Soumaya Museum (free entry, extraordinary collection including works by Rodin and Dalí), and stop at the Jumex Contemporary Art Museum for cutting-edge Latin American art.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Lucha Libre wrestling match at Arena México — a quintessential and electrifying slice of Mexican popular culture. Arrange premium ringside seats through your concierge. Follow with a late dinner at Sud 777, an award-winning modern Mexican restaurant in Pedregal known for its garden setting and inventive tasting menus.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Café Nin in Colonia Juárez — a chic café known for excellent chilaquiles and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Quintonil in Polanco — Chef Jorge Vallejo's celebrated restaurant focusing on indigenous Mexican ingredients and techniques; one of Latin America's top restaurants
meals.dinner: Sud 777 — contemporary Mexican fine dining in a stunning garden setting; tasting menu with natural wine pairing recommended

day_by_day.notes: Lucha Libre matches at Arena México typically start at 7:30 PM on Fridays. Confirm the schedule with your concierge. Book Quintonil well in advance — it is one of the most sought-after reservations in the city.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul — the Blue House) in Coyoacán, the cobblestoned bohemian neighborhood where Frida Kahlo was born and lived. Book a timed-entry VIP ticket in advance. Explore the charming Jardín Centenario plaza and the Mercado de Coyoacán for artisan crafts and local snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Centro Histórico for a private mezcal and tequila masterclass at a premium mezcalería such as La Clandestina or Expendio de Pulques Finos. Learn about the distillation traditions of Oaxacan mezcal and Jalisco tequila, guided by a certified spirits sommelier. Spend the final hours browsing the artisan markets near the Zócalo for curated souvenirs — silver jewelry, Talavera ceramics, and handwoven textiles.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Rosetta, Chef Elena Reygadas's flagship restaurant in Colonia Roma — a converted 1906 mansion serving refined Italian-Mexican cuisine with the finest seasonal local ingredients. End the evening with a nightcap at the rooftop bar of your hotel, toasting the final night in one of the world's great cities.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely in-hotel breakfast or brunch at El Cardenal in Centro Histórico — an institution for traditional Mexican breakfast dishes including tamales, atole, and pan dulce
meals.lunch: Lunch at Los Danzantes in Coyoacán — excellent modern Oaxacan cuisine with a beautiful terrace setting and outstanding mezcal selection
meals.dinner: Rosetta — one of Mexico City's most beloved fine-dining restaurants; seasonal tasting menu with natural wine pairing in a romantic mansion setting

day_by_day.notes: La Casa Azul requires advance timed-entry tickets — book online at least 2 weeks ahead as slots sell out quickly. Allow extra time in Coyoacán as the neighborhood is highly walkable and full of character. Confirm checkout time and arrange airport transfer for the following morning if departing early.
